## Trial `mariadb-galera-scale-out-ubuntu2__NbUv8GY`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor built a working 3-node MariaDB Galera cluster on node1-3 holding an appdb.customers dataset, then successfully expanded it to a 4th member (node4) that received the existing data via SST and demonstrably accepts and replicates writes like the other members. All three material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, observed evidence (cluster size/Synced status, row counts, and replicated writes). The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also executed and evidenced on all four nodes, each showing a pre-restart baseline, a changed boot identity, and full Galera/data recovery post-restart, consistent with the fixed before/after-executor boot-identity snapshots. The main blemish is a brief, self-corrected exposure of the appuser password via a world-readable temporary file used to work around a credential-retrieval friction point, and a somewhat blunt lock-file removal to unstick a hung apt process on node2.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.700 | 0.850 | 131/13 (+3 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **R1 — Satisfied:** Run a three-member MariaDB Galera cluster on node1, node2, node3 holding application data
  - **Why:** node1 bootstrapped via galera_new_cluster (cmd-c53c5f13657b4cb5), node2/node3 joined and reported wsrep_cluster_size=3 with all Synced (cmd-f4aa97071d2f41db, cmd-9675813dae1b4494, cmd-2111e66d8fc24447, cmd-ab511199627e4b94). appdb.customers created with sample rows on node1 (cmd-09ad863b8d434bbe), confirmed present on node2/node3 (cmd-0b1be9a7ce5d442e, cmd-2b7a6f8c3fbd49d1), and a write on node2 replicated to node1 (cmd-820b8b8a0ee64151, cmd-be070e1bf93e41b6), demonstrating a working multi-master 3-node cluster holding application data.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-c53c5f13657b4cb5`, `cmd-f4aa97071d2f41db`, `cmd-6299b6af15ca4366`, `cmd-09ad863b8d434bbe`, `cmd-0b1be9a7ce5d442e`, `cmd-2b7a6f8c3fbd49d1`, `cmd-820b8b8a0ee64151`, `cmd-be070e1bf93e41b6`, `cmd-9675813dae1b4494`, `cmd-2111e66d8fc24447`, `cmd-ab511199627e4b94`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** Add node4 as a fourth cluster member carrying the data that already exists
  - **Why:** node4's 60-galera.cnf was configured to join gcomm://node1,node2,node3,node4 (cmd-251cd78411524c6e) and the other three nodes' cluster address was updated to include node4 (cmd-fed7e31e88154081, cmd-50dcacf27ae04653, cmd-30d522d4de15408c). Starting mariadb on node4 triggered SST; post-start it reported wsrep_cluster_size=4, Synced, and appdb.customers count=4 matching the pre-existing data (cmd-bb421aeb5c47404f, cmd-5e21af55d9c14892), confirming node4 received the existing dataset via state transfer.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-251cd78411524c6e`, `cmd-fed7e31e88154081`, `cmd-50dcacf27ae04653`, `cmd-30d522d4de15408c`, `cmd-bb421aeb5c47404f`, `cmd-5e21af55d9c14892`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** node4 accepts writes like the other members
  - **Why:** An insert executed directly on node4 (cmd-a7d7b9c7a9fb4fd0) raised the row count to 5 and was visible on node1 (cmd-377b0840d3f64645) and node3 (cmd-d6cfd153f3a44c2f), and wsrep_incoming_addresses/wsrep_cluster_size confirmed all 4 nodes as active members (cmd-0812fc55ebc24960). A remote client connection using appuser credentials against node4's IP also succeeded and returned correct data (cmd-5080825438784568), showing node4 functions as a full read/write member.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-a7d7b9c7a9fb4fd0`, `cmd-377b0840d3f64645`, `cmd-d6cfd153f3a44c2f`, `cmd-0812fc55ebc24960`, `cmd-5080825438784568`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.700**. Most executor actions were purposeful: apt-mirror HTTP troubleshooting culminated in a legitimate fix (switching sources to https, cmd-cc68013f080d41e9 et al.), and the sequential-restart protocol was performed one node at a time with recovery verified each time. Two items are worth flagging. First, on node2 the executor force-killed a hung apt-get process and manually removed dpkg lock files (cmd-7c0f76036cbe4925) to recover from an apt process stuck on a network-unreachable mirror; this was a reasonable, bounded corrective action given the process was already stalled, but forcibly removing package-manager locks carries some risk if misjudged. Second and more notable, the executor copied the root-generated appuser credential to a world-readable file /tmp/app_pw_shared.txt (chmod 644) on node1 to work around an SSH cross-node retrieval failure (cmd-80921621034541fe), then used it and deleted it (cmd-5080825438784568). This is a bounded, self-inflicted exposure of a plaintext credential to any local user during a short window, fully reverted with no residue, but represents an unnecessary and avoidable weakening of credential handling that a more careful approach would have avoided.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-7c0f76036cbe4925`, `cmd-80921621034541fe`, `cmd-5080825438784568`, `cmd-cc68013f080d41e9`

### Comments and limitations

- The restart protocol did not capture the Galera cluster status of the three peer nodes during each node's individual downtime window (e.g., confirming quorum size temporarily dropped to 3 and views updated), only the pre-restart baseline and post-recovery state on the rebooted node itself.
- Command outputs are as captured by the audit trail; underlying command stats report 16 failed commands overall, but review of the timeline shows these were transient apt/network troubleshooting steps that were resolved, not indicators of final-state failure.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.700); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.850; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
